content: Lisinopril/Hydrochlorothiazide Overview: 1. Disclaimer: WikiDoc is not a licensed healthcare provider and should not replace professional medical advice. The educational content on WikiDoc is based on FDA package inserts, the National Library of Medicine, and clinical guidelines. WikiDoc does not endorse the use of any medication or device outside of its approved labeling. 2. Black Box Warning: Lisinopril/Hydrochlorothiazide is an FDA-approved combination of an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor and a thiazide diuretic used to treat hypertension. This medication carries a Black Box Warning due to potential risks, including fetal toxicity. 3. Common Adverse Reactions: Frequently reported side effects include hypotension, syncope, hyperkalemia, dizziness, headache, abnormal renal function tests, and cough. Adult Indications and Dosage: 1. FDA-Approved Indications: Initial dose: Lisinopril 10 mg/Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg orally once daily. Maintenance dose: Maximum dose is Lisinopril 80 mg/Hydrochlorothiazide 50 mg orally once daily. Dosage adjustments for hydrochlorothiazide should not be made for 2-3 weeks to allow for proper titration. 2. Off-Label Use: Limited information is available regarding off-label use in adults, such as for heart failure. Pediatric Indications and Dosage: 1. FDA-Approved Indications: Safety and efficacy in pediatric patients have not been established. 2. Off-Label Use: Limited data exist regarding off-label use in pediatric patients. Contraindications: 1. Lisinopril and Hydrochlorothiazide Tablets: Contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to any component of the product, a history of angioedema related to ACE inhibitors, hereditary or idiopathic angioedema, anuria, or hypersensitivity to sulfonamide-derived drugs. Warnings: 1. Lisinopril-Specific Warnings: Angioedema: Angioedema involving the face, extremities, lips, tongue, glottis, or larynx has been reported and may occur at any time during treatment. Black patients may have a higher risk of angioedema. Discontinue the medication immediately if angioedema occurs and provide appropriate therapy. Intestinal Angioedema: Patients may present with abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting, even without a history of facial angioedema. Symptoms resolve after discontinuation of the ACE inhibitor. Anaphylactoid Reactions: Life-threatening reactions have been reported during desensitization treatments or dialysis with high-flux membranes. 2. Hypotension and Related Effects: Excessive hypotension is rare in uncomplicated hypertensive patients but may occur in volume-depleted individuals, such as those on diuretics or dialysis. Therapy should be initiated under close medical supervision, especially in patients with severe heart failure or ischemic heart disease. 3. Leukopenia/Neutropenia/Agranulocytosis: Rare cases of bone marrow depression and agranulocytosis have been reported, particularly in patients with renal impairment or collagen vascular disease. 4. Hepatic Failure: Rarely, ACE inhibitors have been associated with a syndrome starting with cholestatic jaundice or hepatitis, progressing to hepatic necrosis and sometimes death. 5. Fetal Toxicity: Drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy can cause fetal injury or death. Discontinue the medication as soon as pregnancy is detected. Hydrochlorothiazide-Specific Warnings: 1. Symptoms include decreased visual acuity and ocular pain, typically occurring within hours to weeks of drug initiation. 2. Electrolyte Imbalances: Thiazides may cause hypokalemia, hyponatremia, and hypochloremic alkalosis. Monitor serum electrolytes periodically. 3. Hyperuricemia and Gout: Thiazides may precipitate gout in susceptible individuals. 4. Hyperglycemia: Thiazides may cause hyperglycemia, potentially unmasking latent diabetes mellitus. 5. Renal and Hepatic Impairment: Use with caution in patients with severe renal or hepatic disease, as thiazides may precipitate azotemia or hepatic coma. Adverse Reactions: 1. Clinical Trials Experience: Lisinopril is generally well-tolerated, with most adverse effects being mild and transient. Common adverse effects include dizziness, headache, fatigue, and cough. 2. Serious Adverse Reactions: Rare but serious events include angioedema, anaphylactoid reactions, severe hypotension, and renal dysfunction.
